judgements.referenceQuote: is a Nigerian economist who has been serving as the director-general of the World Trade Organization since March 2021. She is the first ever woman and also the first African to lead the World Trade Organization as director-general.
judgements.evidenceQuote: In 2021, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala became the first African and first woman appointed director-general of the World Trade Organization (WTO).
judgements.rationale: The dossier states the same fact — first woman and first African WTO director-general — but only dates it to 2021, not to March 2021 as the reference does.

judgements.referenceQuote: She also previously sat on the Twitter Board of Directors, and stepped down in February 2021 in connection with her appointment as director-general of the World Trade Organization.
judgements.evidenceQuote: She also sits on the Boards of Standard Chartered PLC and Twitter Inc.
judgements.rationale: The dossier asserts she currently sits on Twitter's board, which is incompatible with the reference fact that she stepped down from the board in February 2021; no departure is mentioned anywhere in the dossier.

judgements.referenceQuote: As Managing Director, she had oversight responsibility for the World Bank’s $81 billion operational portfolio in Africa, South Asia, Europe, and Central Asia.
judgements.rationale: The dossier only notes she was a World Bank managing director between 2007 and 2011; it never mentions the $81 billion operational portfolio or the regions (Africa, South Asia, Europe and Central Asia) it covered.

judgements.referenceQuote: In 2010, she chaired the IDA replenishment, the World Bank’s successful drive to raise $49.3 billion in grants and low-interest credit for the world's poorest country.
judgements.rationale: No dossier statement mentions her chairing the 2010 IDA replenishment or the $49.3 billion raised in grants and low-interest credit.

judgements.referenceQuote: During her first tenure as Finance Minister in the administration of President Olusegun Obasanjo, she spearheaded negotiations with the Paris Club that led to the elimination of US$30 billion of Nigeria's debt, including the outright cancellation of US$18 billion.
judgements.evidenceQuote: She worked to free her country from 30 billion dollars of debt owed to the Paris Club
judgements.rationale: The dossier states the $30 billion Paris Club debt relief effort, but omits that she led the negotiations during her first finance-minister term and does not mention the $18 billion outright cancellation component.

judgements.referenceQuote: When she takes office on 1 March , Dr Okonjo-Iweala will become the first woman and the first African to be chosen as Director-General. Her term, renewable, will expire on 31 August 2025.
judgements.evidenceQuote: In 2021, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala became the first African and first woman appointed director-general of the World Trade Organization (WTO).
judgements.rationale: The dossier covers only the first-woman/first-African element of the appointment record; it does not state the 1 March taking of office, the welcome by General Council Chair David Walker, or the nine-month selection process.

judgements.referenceQuote: Paris Club creditors agree in principle on a comprehensive debt treatment for Nigeria
judgements.evidenceQuote: She worked to free her country from 30 billion dollars of debt owed to the Paris Club
judgements.rationale: The dossier states the Paris Club debt relief outcome but does not state the 29 June 2005 agreement in principle on comprehensive debt treatment, nor the noted reform program implemented since 2003 under President Obasanjo.

overclaims.statement: She also sits on the Boards of Standard Chartered PLC and Twitter Inc.
overclaims.citedQuote: She also sits on the Boards of Standard Chartered PLC and Twitter Inc.
overclaims.rationale: The dossier presents a Twitter Inc. board seat as current, but the reference material records her departure from the Twitter board in February 2021; the speakers-bureau bio cited is outdated on this point. The Standard Chartered seat may also be stale but the Twitter claim is the clear error.

overclaims.statement: She stated vaccine inequity during the coronavirus pandemic demonstrates the need for developing nations to be able to make vaccines.
overclaims.rationale: The cited quote is only the truncated fragment 'said Thursday that ' — it contains none of the substance about vaccine inequity or developing-nation vaccine manufacturing, so the specific content of her statement is not supported by the cited passage as given.

overclaims.citedQuote: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is a nonresident distinguished fellow with the Africa Growth Initiative in the Global Economy and Development program at Brookings.
overclaims.rationale: The Brookings profile describes her in the present tense as a nonresident distinguished fellow, but she has been WTO Director-General since March 2021; the Brookings listing appears not to have been updated, so presenting this as a current role likely overstates the citation.

overclaims.citedQuote: She was a member of the board of trustees of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace and the Rockefeller Foundation.
overclaims.rationale: The cited passage says she 'was a member of the board of trustees' — past tense — while the dossier statement phrases this as a current affiliation ('Board trustee'), asserting a present role the passage does not give.

usefulness.rationale: Understanding: The dossier gives a coherent picture of who Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is — WTO Director-General (first woman and first African in the role, since 2021), two-time Nigerian finance minister (2003–2006, 2011–2015), brief foreign minister, 25-year World Bank career rising to Managing Director, Harvard/MIT education, Gavi board chair, Lazard advisor, and her policy positions on WTO reform and vaccine equity. Multiple independent sources (MIT News, TED, Brookings, PBS, Guardian, Wikipedia) corroborate the core facts. RemainingQuestions: The dossier never states what it does not know — there are no explicit gaps, caveats, or "unknown" fields; the supported/contested/claimed statuses hint at uncertainty but the dossier implies completeness about her life (e.g., nothing on family, current board seats post-2021, or the reliability of the speakers-bureau material). ConversationReadiness: A reader could comfortably prepare for a meeting: current role and employer, career timeline, education, recognition, and her stated ideas (subsidy/competition reform, developing-country involvement, pandemic and climate public goods) are all present and cited.
